pr_title: fix: Raise if scan zstd compressed csv file

issue_context.title: `scan_csv` reads column names incorrectly from compressed files
issue_context.body:
### Checks

- [X] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.

- [X] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pypi.org/project/polars/) of Polars.


### Reproducible example

```
echo col1\n1 > /tmp/test.csv && zstd /tmp/test.csv
```

```python
In [1]: import polars as pl

In [2]: pl.read_csv("/tmp/test.csv.zst")
Out[2]:
shape: (1, 1)
┌──────┐
│ col1 │
│ ---  │
│ i64  │
╞══════╡
│ 1    │
└──────┘

In [3]: pl.scan_csv("/tmp/test.csv.zst")
Out[3]: <LazyFrame [1 col, {"(�/�$9col1": Utf8}] at 0x1073B0350>
```


### Log output

_No response_

### Issue description

`scan_csv` reads compressed bytes as  column names, while `read_csv` works.

### Expected behavior

Should either error or work as expected

comments: We should error. `scan_csv` doesn't support compressed files.
We can't scan compressed csv file. But as the wrong use of `start_with`, `zstd` was incorrectly allowed (:.

review_comments: Since we now have 4 bytes magic number(for `zstd`), this may be a necessary cost (reading two more bytes than before). Or do we have other better ways?
That's essentially free. So seems fine. :)
